{"parentUuid":"a0e16916-652d-4995-9e3e-77e800b3ad29","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"mcp_instructions_delta","addedNames":["plugin:context7:context7","plugin:serena:serena"],"addedBlocks":["## plugin:context7:context7\nUse this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service -- even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer -- your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.\n\nDo not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.","## plugin:serena:serena\nCRITICAL: Before starting to work on a coding task, call the `initial_instructions` tool to read the 'Serena Instructions Manual'."],"removedNames":[]},"type":"attachment","uuid":"6aedfbcd-1569-499d-8749-6f91346f1ead","timestamp":"2026-05-07T01:19:30.450Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"ef9a1c57-23ae-436e-ac00-422b2e1014c5","version":"2.1.124","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"6aedfbcd-1569-499d-8749-6f91346f1ead","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- empirical-probe-first: Probe ALL viable strategies in a multi-option ladder BEFORE committing to one. Use when a session-plan / decision-ADR / spec presents ≥3 strategy options (e.g. \"Strategy A1/A2/A3\" or \"alternative B/C/D\") and the recommended option's source-evidence may be stale. Outputs a probe matrix per strategy + commit decision with empirical citation. Pairs with `vendor-api-probe.sh` (deterministic detection layer; SessionStart hook) and `decompose-work` (deterministic-vs-LLM split per probe). Charter promotion target — codifies L-S32-1 doctrine surfaced at S32 Track A pivot (master-plan recommended A2 vnstock alternate; empirical probe rejected A1+A2; A3 SSI direct httpx adopted instead).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use during sandwich-verifier review, drift investigation, or post-mortem when component-telemetry.jsonl + dispatch.jsonl + sessions-rollup.tsv need cross-checking.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- sync-pull: On-demand confidence-score lookup before a SCOPE+/ARCH/IMPL decision. Reads agent-workspace/memory/sync-tracker/state.tsv + weights.yaml; surfaces the relevant category's score, tier, must-grill flag, and the decision-class threshold. Output drives \"self-decide vs grill\" choice. Use whenever an agent is about to commit a non-trivial decision and needs to ground confidence in historical hit rate per Charter Principle 8 (Calibration over confidence).\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. {"parentUuid":"3dd6e212-cb13-412f-bb5e-f0f1f26b9b26","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"nested_memory","path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\CLAUDE.md","content":{"path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\CLAUDE.md","type":"Project","content":"# agent-workspace/ — Contract\n\n> **Audience**: agents working inside `agent-workspace/`.\n> **Established**: Decision 002 § Track 1 (Workspace Dualism Foundation).\n\n## Identity\n\n`agent-workspace/` is the **agent-owned execution + memory** layer. Everything here represents **agent state, decisions, plans, observations, learning**. Agents WRITE here freely (within constitution rules); humans READ here but normally do not edit.\n\nThis separation exists to prevent two failure modes from orch:\n1. **Charter drift via shared-workspace mutation** (orch CF-DOGFOOD-2)\n2. **Human cognitive overload from dense session logs** (UP02 §1.3 — \"human đối mặt hàng chục spec/document quá tải nếu không sắp xếp khoa học\")\n\nThe agent owns this directory but must keep it AUDITABLE — every artifact provenance-linked, every decision sourced.\n\n---\n\n## Subdirectories\n\n| Path | Purpose | Lifecycle |\n|---|---|---|\n| `constitution/` | **IMMUTABLE without explicit user approval**. Charter-tier rules (autonomous-protocol, model-routing, identity-scope, etc.). Track 7 produces drafts in `proposals/`; user explicit approve to move here. | Edit denied by .claude/settings.json; Write only via human approval gate |\n| `memory/project.md` | High-level project state; phase tracker; ADRs (last 5). Update on phase boundaries + architectural decisions. | Long-lived; trim to most recent decisions |\n| `memory/current-execution.md` | **THE single routing source of truth**. Active phase + active session + autonomous_mode flag + routing table. Read FIRST every session. | Long-lived; updated each session boundary |\n| `memory/agent-notes.md` | Learned rules from real experience (post-mortem / drift / user correction). Append-only mostly. | Long-lived |\n| `memory/decisions/` | Sequential ADRs (`NNN-<slug>.md`) + `_template.md` + `README.md` index. 12-field schema (Track 2). | Append-only; supersession via status field |\n| `memory/sessions/` | One file per session: `YYYY-MM-DD-session-N.md`. What happened, decisions made, files touched. | Append-only |\n| `memory/observations/` | Subagent return artifacts (per Track 6 spec). Each subagent writes one observation file describing what it did. | Append; cleaned periodically by aggregator |\n| `memory/checkpoints/` | Session handoff state for self-reboot (Track 5). `latest.md` is canonical pointer; timestamped historical files retained. | Append + latest.md updated each checkpoint |\n| `memory/patterns-discovered/` | Pattern mining outputs (Track 0 — DONE) + ongoing pattern catalog. | Append; significant patterns promoted to constitution |\n| `memory/drift-logs/` | Drift-check (DR1-DR12) results; runs on hook + on-demand. | Time-series append |\n| `memory/post-mortems/` | After significant failure or thesis-revoked event: what failed, root cause, prevention rule. | Append |\n| `memory/thesis-log/` | Stock-domain thesis exploration entries. Read-only for IMPL sessions. | Append + revisited per calibration |\n| `memory/sync-tracker/` | Track 8a output: Confidence Score SQLite + weights.yaml + auto-rendered `_index.md`. | Live updated by hooks |\n| `memory/self-awareness/` | Track 9 output: model × effort × thinking profile cards + known-issues + best-practices. | Live updated by Stop-hook aggregator |\n| `memory/mistake-log.md` | Track 7 deliverable: structured failure catalog. What went wrong / Root cause / Prevention rule / Severity. | Append; pre-flight read by all agents |\n| `session-plans/pending/` | Plans authored, awaiting execution. Phase 0 plan lives here. | Move to `completed/` when done |\n| `session-plans/completed/` | Executed plans; archived for reference + retrospective input. | Append |\n| `quality-reports/{deterministic,probabilistic,drift-reports}/` | Tier-1/2/3 gate outputs (CLAUDE.md § Quality Gates). | Per-run files |\n| `ubiquitous-language/` | DDD glossary + domain-mapping + drift-log. Stockforge stock-domain vocabulary. | Append; canonical via `/drill-me` |\n| `calibration/` | Empirical hit-rate data per signal type. Confidence claims MUST trace here (CLAUDE.md hard rule). | Append per thesis post-mortem |\n| `research/` | Research notes from `research-scanner` subagent dispatches (e.g., reference-repo studies). | Append |\n\n---\n\n## Contract Rules (BINDING)\n\n1. **Constitution is immutable absent explicit human approval.** `Edit/Write` to `agent-workspace/constitution/**` is in `.claude/settings.json` deny list. Track 7 writes constitution drafts to `proposals/`; user explicit approve moves them.\n\n2. **`memory/decisions/` is append-mostly + supersession-status.** Don't delete decisions; mark `status: superseded-by-D-NNN` to revoke. Sequential numbering (`001`, `002`, ...) — don't reuse numbers.\n\n3. **`current-execution.md` is the routing source-of-truth.** No skill, agent, or command may hardcode phase paths or session paths from memory; resolve via this file. Stale paths in CLAUDE.md or skills = anti-pattern.\n\n4. **Never edit `obsidian-vault/raw/`.** Immutable. Vault writes only to `wiki/`. (Established in stockforge CLAUDE.md.)\n\n5. **Provenance is mandatory.** Every decision file references its source (human prompt / spec clause / drift detection / agent inference). Every thesis cites source + as-of date (I-S2). Every confidence claim cites historical hit rate (I-S20-equivalent).\n\n6. **Agents never `git commit` in this directory unless user explicitly requests.** Stage only.\n\n7. **`patterns-discovered/` artifacts are READ-ONLY for production code.** Patterns must be promoted to constitution / skills / hook scripts before becoming binding. (Otherwise they're informal notes, not contracts.)\n\n---\n\n## Reading Priority for Agent\n\nPer `agent-workspace/constitution/autonomous-protocol.md` (Track 7) and stockforge `CLAUDE.md` § Session Protocol:\n\n1. **`memory/current-execution.md`** — first; resolve active track\n2. **`memory/project.md`** — project state\n3. **`memory/checkpoints/latest.md`** if a recent checkpoint exists (within last 24h) — resume context\n4. **`memory/agent-notes.md`** — learned rules\n5. **`memory/mistake-log.md`** — pre-flight failure catalog\n6. **Last 3 files in `memory/sessions/`** — recent context\n7. **`session-plans/pending/<active-plan>.md`** — current plan\n8. **Relevant constitution files** as task demands (don't load all every session)\n9. **Relevant skills + agents + commands** as task demands\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Patterns to Avoid\n\n(From `memory/patterns-discovered/SYNTHESIS.md` § 6, full catalog 23 items. Highest-priority for this directory:)\n\n- **AP-1 Same-agent self-review** — never review your own implementation; dispatch fresh-context verifier\n- **AP-2 Self-track wind-down** — `.transcript-tokens` real-transcript is authoritative, not LLM self-track\n- **AP-5 Charter-coherence defer overriding user-CRITICAL** — re-read all `user_prompt/*` at every phase entry; never silently defer USER-CRITICAL\n- **AP-7 Performative SC ticking** — defer with explicit prerequisites > fire vacuous proposals\n- **AP-8 Pre-staged work causing checkpoint drift** — update `current-execution.md` immediately on task complete, not session-end\n- **AP-17 Identity drift** — stockforge is AI-first VN stock advisory; not generic financial framework (see `constitution/identity-scope.md` once Track 7 ships)\n- **AP-23 Continuous LLM-Guardian** — deterministic hooks = Guardian; LLM Guardian only at session-end aggregation\n\n---\n\n## Connection to human-workspace/\n\nThis directory is the agent's domain. Human's domain is `human-workspace/`. The two communicate through:\n- Human → Agent: `human-workspace/user_prompt/`, `human-workspace/decisions/`\n- Agent → Human: `human-workspace/notifications/`, `human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/`\n- Bidirectional: `human-workspace/q-and-a/answered/` — agent writes pending; either human or agent (per Auto-mv rule below) moves resolved bundles to answered/\n- Audit trail: this directory's `memory/decisions/` references `human-workspace/` source files via path pointers\n\n**Auto-mv rule (HH-E.2 — D-031 ratification, 2026-05-05)**: Agent MAY mv a bundle from `q-and-a/pending/` to `q-and-a/answered/` IFF ALL of the following hold:\n\n1. **Frontmatter signal**: bundle frontmatter `status:` field value starts with one of: `answered-`, `closed-`, `resolved-`. Examples already in repo: `answered-via-chat`, `answered-via-AskUserQuestion`, `answered-2026-05-04-via-chat`. Detection is deterministic (head -20 of file + grep `^status:`).\n2. **No human-veto signal**: bundle frontmatter has NO `wait_until:` ISO-8601 timestamp greater than current epoch — if present, agent MUST defer mv until that timestamp passes. Allows human to override auto-mv per-bundle without contract amendment.\n3. **No global pause**: file `human-workspace/q-and-a/.auto-mv-paused` does NOT exist — global kill switch for the auto-mv mechanism (single empty file presence pauses all auto-mv).\n4. **Hook validation**: the mv is performed by `scripts/hooks/qa-pending-auto-mover.sh` (Stop hook). Direct manual `mv` invocation by agent (e.g. via Bash tool) is STILL forbidden — only the validated hook path is authorized.\n\nAgent never writes to `human-workspace/` outside the designated `q-and-a/pending/` write channel + the auto-mv rule above + `notifications/` write channel (existing).\n","contentDiffersFromDisk":false},"displayPath":"agent-workspace\\CLAUDE.md"},"type":"attachment","uuid":"c0185266-8520-451a-9db4-3513543dde69","timestamp":"2026-05-07T01:19:45.828Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"ef9a1c57-23ae-436e-ac00-422b2e1014c5","version":"2.1.124","gitBranch":"main"}

Everything here represents **human decisions, scope, intent, and verification**. Agents READ this directory as authoritative; agents do NOT WRITE here except in one designated channel (`q-and-a/pending/` — where agents post questions for human to answer).\n\nThis separation exists because of a failure mode observed in the orch sister project (orch `decisions/040`, post-mortem CF-DOGFOOD-2): when human and agent share a single workspace without contract, agent silently overrides human-CRITICAL items via technical-defer logic. The user explicitly raised this concern in `human-workspace/user_prompt/20260429_02_init.txt` §1.1.\n\n---\n\n## Subdirectories\n\n| Path | Purpose | Who writes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `user_prompt/` | Human's mid-flight scope/idea drops. Naming: `YYYYMMDD_NN_<slug>.txt`. Files are immutable post-creation (audit trail). | **Human only**. Agent: read-only. |\n| `decisions/` | Human's strategic decisions (e.g., scope-lock, charter-revision-trigger, peer-share authorization). Format: `D-H-<NNN>-<slug>.md`. | **Human only**. Agent: read-only. |\n| `q-and-a/pending/` | **The ONE channel where agent writes inside human-workspace**. Levels: INFO / SUMMARY / ALERT. | **Agent writes**; human reads. |\n\n---\n\n## Contract Rules (BINDING)\n\n1. **Agent NEVER writes to `user_prompt/` or `decisions/`.** Permission deny. If something feels like a human decision but the human hasn't written it, dispatch a Q&A bundle into `q-and-a/pending/` instead.\n\n2. **`user_prompt/` files are immutable post-creation.** Agent never deletes, renames, or edits these files. They are the audit trail of human interventions.\n\n3. **Q&A bundle format** (per Track 4 spec): YAML frontmatter (`id`, `topic`, `opened_at`, `expected_answer_by`, `priority`, `related_decisions`, `status`) + question body + answer-fill section. Each bundle = up to 25 questions per Grill Maximization doctrine; split if more.\n\n4. **Agent does not move files between `q-and-a/{pending,answered,stale}/`** — that's human's role (or hook's, in case of stale). Agent only WRITES new pending bundles and READS answers.\n\n5. **Notifications are read-only for human.** Human shouldn't edit `notifications/*` files; if disagreement with notification content, drop a `user_prompt/` instead. Notifications are the agent's account of events.\n\n6. **Provenance pointers**: every `agent-workspace/memory/decisions/D-<NNN>` should reference its source `human-workspace/user_prompt/<file>` or `human-workspace/decisions/D-H-<NNN>` if the agent's decision derives from human input.\n\n7. **No multi-tenancy in this directory.** Per identity-scope.md (Track 7), stockforge is single-tenant Phase 0-5; if peer share happens it's via git-fork, each peer has their own `human-workspace/` per fork.\n\n---\n\n## Reading Priority for Agent\n\nWhen loading session context (per `agent-workspace/constitution/autonomous-protocol.md` Track 7):\n\n1. **All `user_prompt/*.txt`** — every prompt, not just most recent. Per orch lesson (decision-040 USER-CRITICAL tier): never silently defer human-CRITICAL items.\n2. **All `decisions/*.md`** — human's strategic decisions are above charter principles in priority; charter is below human (charter was authored by human in the first place).\n3. **Latest `q-and-a/answered/*`** — recent answers update agent's understanding.\n4. **Open `q-and-a/pending/*`** — flag if waiting on human answers.\n5. **Recent `notifications/*`** (last 7 days) — for situational awareness.\n\n---\n\n## Agent Self-Check\n\nBefore writing to `human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/`, ask:\n- Is this question genuinely something the human must decide? (Charter principle / Charter-affecting / SCOPE-affecting / above ARCH-tier confidence threshold)\n- Have I already grilled this in a recent bundle? (Don't ask twice; don't pollute pending/)\n- Am I bundling per Grill Maximization (target 15-20 questions, max 25)? Or splintering across many small bundles?\n\nIf the answer to any is \"I'm not sure\" — DON'T write the bundle. {"parentUuid":"878a6fab-9e00-4192-ae48-924a0182b75a","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01LxHXwDQAEMBU1XusGznnMd","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Xtbf9SYWYjwCkTZJYdzQx2","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\memory\\observations\\2026-05-07-S176-HH-C2-misfire-root-cause.md","content":"---\nobservation_id: 2026-05-07-S176-HH-C2-misfire-root-cause\ntype: focused-audit\nsession: S176\nphase: 3.5\ncreated_at: 2026-05-07T08:25:00+07:00\nrelated_decisions: D-038-PROPOSED\nrelated_mistakes: M-S176-1\nrelated_lessons: L-S176-1\nstatus: COMPLETE\nverdict: HOOK-IS-DOUBLE-BROKEN-NO-OP-SINCE-INCEPTION\nseverity: HIGH\n---\n\n# HH-C.2 Staleness Watchdog Misfire — Root-Cause Audit\n\n> S175 checkpoint S176 NEXT ACTION PRIORITY 1: investigate why `project-md-staleness-check.sh` Stop hook existed but project.md still slipped 2 days × 5 ADRs pre-S172.\n\n## Verdict (one-line)\n\n**Hook is a double-broken no-op since 2026-05-06 inception (commit 13e5535)** — Check A regex never matches `current-execution.md` actual format + Check B file glob never matches actual ADR filenames. Zero WARN entries across 10836 log lines = expected behavior of a hook that always silently exits with `WARN_COUNT=0`.\n\n## Hypotheses tested\n\nS175 checkpoint enumerated four hypotheses (H1-H4). Audit added H5 after empirical inspection of file naming convention.\n\n| ID | Hypothesis | Status | Evidence |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| H1 | Stop hook silent on Windows per M-S49b-1 | **REJECTED** | `.session-hooks.log` shows other Stop hooks firing today (S175 close 08:19:21+): `SessionEnd`, `session-export-raw`, `working-memory-budget-audit`. If Stop chain were Windows-silent, NO Stop hook would log. |\n| H2 | Hour-bucket marker collision masked legitimate fires | **RESOLVED-POST-L-S108-1** | Current marker `agent-workspace/memory/.project-md-staleness-fired-20260507-08` shows hour-bucket format working as designed. Cleanup-stale-markers loop (lines 37-43) intact. L-S108-1 fix shipped at S109 prevented per-session-lockout. |\n| H3 | Hook regex pattern too narrow (Check A) | **CONFIRMED** | Hook line 60-61: `grep -m1 -E '^\\*\\*Phase\\*\\*:[[:space:]]*[0-9]'` against `current-execution.md` returns NOTHING. Actual format uses section headers `## SNNN — Phase X.Y — ...` (e.g., `## S175 — Phase 3.5 — FOCUSED_IMPL-DONE: ...`). NO `**Phase**: N` line exists anywhere in the file. → `ACTIVE_PHASE=\"\"` → entire Check A block (lines 63-97) silently skipped on every invocation. |\n| H4 | project-md-staleness-check thresholds too lax | **IRRELEVANT** | Threshold `>2.0h` (line 115) is sane but never reached because Check B exits early via H5 (no NEWEST_ADR detected). |\n| **H5 NEW** | **Check B file glob `D-*.md` doesn't match actual ADR naming `NNN-*.md`** | **CONFIRMED** | Hook line 104: `find \"$DECISIONS_DIR\" -maxdepth 1 -name 'D-*.md' -type f`. Empirical test returns EMPTY because actual filenames are `037-S175-M-S171-1-prevention-hooks.md`, NOT `D-037-...md`. The `D-NNN` IS the ADR ID inside file frontmatter + content + project.md table, but file PREFIX is bare `NNN-`. Confirmed by `ls agent-workspace/memory/decisions/` — all 38 files (001..037 + _template.md) start with digits, none with literal `D-`. → `NEWEST_ADR_TS=\"\"` → entire Check B block (lines 109-122) silently skipped on every invocation. |\n\n## Empirical evidence\n\n### Test 1 — Stop hook chain DOES fire on Windows (rejects H1)\n\n```\n$ tail -30 agent-workspace/memory/.session-hooks.log\n[2026-05-07T08:19:21+07:00] SessionEnd session=\n[2026-05-07T08:19:22+07:00] session-export-raw: wrote .../2026-05-07-session-175.md\n[2026-05-07T08:19:23+07:00] SessionStart session= cwd=/c/htdocs/stockforge\n... (working-memory-budget-audit, sync-grilling-trigger, learning-queue-sweeper, etc.)\n```\n\nStop chain ran at 08:19:21 (S175 close); SessionStart chain ran at 08:19:23. Both fire. project-md-staleness-check is in Stop chain (`.claude/settings.json` line 383) → it ran but produced WARN_COUNT=0 → no log line.\n\n### Test 2 — Check A regex empirical (confirms H3)\n\n```bash\n$ grep -m1 -E '^\\*\\*Phase\\*\\*:' agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md\n(no output; exit 1)\n\n$ grep -m1 -oE '## S[0-9]+ — Phase [0-9.]+' agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md\n## S175 — Phase 3.5\n```\n\nThe hook's regex finds nothing; the alternate regex (matching actual format) extracts `Phase 3.5` correctly.\n\n### Test 3 — Check B glob empirical (confirms H5)\n\n```bash\n$ find agent-workspace/memory/decisions -maxdepth 1 -name 'D-*.md' -type f -printf '%T@\\t%f\\n' | sort -rn | head -1\n(empty; exit 1 from find)\n\n$ ls agent-workspace/memory/decisions/ | head -10\n_template.md\n001-orch-vs-cc-native.md\n002-phase-0-harness-bootstrap-design.md\n...\n037-S175-M-S171-1-prevention-hooks.md\n\n$ find agent-workspace/memory/decisions -maxdepth 1 -regextype posix-extended -regex '.*/[0-9]+-.*\\.md' -type f -printf '%T@\\t%f\\n' | sort -rn | head -1\n1778116369.3867873000\t037-S175-M-S171-1-prevention-hooks.md\n```\n\nThe hook's `D-*.md` glob returns empty; corrected `[0-9]+-.*\\.md` regex finds the newest ADR.\n\n### Test 4 — Zero WARN entries across hook lifetime (corroborates double-broken)\n\n```bash\n$ wc -l agent-workspace/memory/.session-hooks.log\n10836\n\n$ grep -c \"project-md-staleness-check\" agent-workspace/memory/.session-hooks.log\n5  # all 5 are L-S108-1 lint-scan metadata, not actual WARN entries\n\n$ grep \"project-md-staleness-check.*warns=\" agent-workspace/memory/.session-hooks.log\n(no output)\n```\n\nHook only writes to log if `WARN_COUNT > 0` (line 125-127). Zero WARN entries across the full log = hook never produced WARN_COUNT > 0. This is consistent with both Check A and Check B silently skipping on every invocation.\n\n### Test 5 — Counter-factual: would corrected hook have fired pre-S172?\n\nPre-S172 state (per S172 audit observation):\n- project.md last update S48d 2026-05-05 (mtime ~2 days stale)\n- D-029, D-030, D-031, D-032 all written between 2026-05-05 and 2026-05-06 (newer than project.md)\n\nWith CORRECTED Check B glob `[0-9]+-.*\\.md`:\n- `NEWEST_ADR_TS` would be D-032's mtime ≈ 2026-05-06\n- `PROJECT_MTIME` would be 2026-05-05 (S48d update)\n- `DELTA_HOURS` ≈ 24-30h\n- `OVER` = 1 (>2.0h)\n- WARN: \"project.md mtime ~28h older than newest ADR (032-S65-...)\" → WARN_COUNT=1 → log entry\n\n**With corrected hook, the S148-S171 22-session × 2-day slip would have surfaced a Stop-hook WARN every session-end after the first ADR landed without project.md update.**\n\n## Root cause analysis\n\n### File-pattern mismatch class\n\nTwo distinct file-pattern bugs:\n- **Check A**: regex written for a `**Phase**: N` text format that never existed in `current-execution.md`. The author appears to have assumed a key-value frontmatter style; actual file uses prose section headers.\n- **Check B**: glob written for `D-*.md` filename prefix; actual convention is `NNN-*.md` with `D-NNN` as the ADR identifier inside file content (`id:` frontmatter + project.md table). The author conflated ADR identifier (D-NNN) with filename prefix.\n\nBoth bugs share a common root: **hook authored without empirical-firing test against real state**. The Phase 3.5 Hard Rule #2 (every hook ships with companion firing-test) was not in force when this hook was authored at 13e5535 (2026-05-06 09:22; pre-Phase 3.5 entry at S50 2026-05-05 — actually concurrent, but Hard Rule #2 codified later in plan 010-S50).\n\n### Charter-Principle-8 violation latent\n\nCharter Principle 8 (Calibration over confidence) demands deterministic over LLM-Guardian. The hook was designed deterministic — but determinism alone is insufficient if the deterministic logic doesn't match real state. **Verify-Before-Write Protocol** (CLAUDE.md hard rule) for hook authoring should include: (a) `ls` the directory the hook globs against; (b) `grep` the file the hook regex parses; (c) tail-test against known-good + known-bad state.\n\n### Recurrence-class lesson\n\nThis is the SAME pattern as M-S171-1 (idle-loop heuristic too narrow). Both hooks shipped with regex/glob patterns that didn't match actual file inventory. **Lesson: file-pattern hooks MUST validate pattern against real-state inventory before shipping; companion firing-test surfaces this at authoring time.**\n\n## Decision matrix for D-038\n\n| Option | Description | Pros | Cons |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| A — FIX | Patch Check A regex to match `## SNNN — Phase X.Y`; patch Check B glob to `[0-9]+-.*\\.md`; add companion firing-test; keep Stop cadence | Closes the bug verbatim; minimal scope; preserves existing wiring | Stop-only cadence misses real-time drift (which is why S175 phase-status-coherence shipped at UserPromptSubmit cadence) |\n| B — MIGRATE | Move project-md-staleness-check.sh to UserPromptSubmit chain alongside phase-status-coherence; merge Check A into phase-status-coherence; keep Check B (mtime drift) at Stop only | Per-prompt phase coherence; Stop-cadence Check B catches end-session drift | More files churn; Stop hook still produces ADR-staleness warns |\n| C — RETIRE | phase-status-coherence (S175) covers Check A scope; session-end-checklist-linter overlaps Check B scope. Tolerates ≤2h drift; WARNs at >2h.\n#\n# Per D-038 Option E (S176 audit observations/2026-05-07-S176-HH-C2-misfire-root-cause.md):\n#   - Check A (phase mismatch) RETIRED — superseded by phase-status-coherence.sh\n#     at UserPromptSubmit cadence (S175 D-037) with stronger 3-sub-check semantics.\n#   - Check B (project.md mtime vs newest ADR) RETAINED + glob FIXED.\n#     Original glob `D-*.md` matched ZERO files (actual ADR naming `NNN-*.md`); fixed\n#     to accept both `[0-9][0-9][0-9]-*.md` (production primary) AND `D-*.md` (backward\n#     compat) via combined find -name clause.\n#\n# Per L-S108-1: hour-bucket marker (no fallback constant; cleanup-stale-markers loop).\n# Per L-S11-1 + UP-05: bash + POSIX tools only.\n# Per Phase 3.5 Hard Rule #2: companion firing-test at firing-tests/project-md-adr-staleness-fire-test.sh\n# uses REAL-STATE-DERIVED fixtures (NNN-*.md naming) per L-S176-1.\n#\n# Soft-warn exit 0 always; never blocks Stop chain.\n\nset -uo pipefail\ntrap 'exit 0' ERR\n\nPROJECT_DIR=\"${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}\"\nSID=\"${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID:-unknown}\"\nMEMORY_DIR=\"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory\"\nPROJECT_MD=\"$MEMORY_DIR/project.md\"\nDECISIONS_DIR=\"$MEMORY_DIR/decisions\"\nHOOK_LOG=\"$MEMORY_DIR/.session-hooks.log\"\nADR_STALENESS_LOG=\"$MEMORY_DIR/.adr-staleness.log\"\nTS=\"$(date -Iseconds 2>/dev/null || date '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S')\"\nTOLERANCE_HOURS=\"2.0\"\n\nmkdir -p \"$MEMORY_DIR\" 2>/dev/null || true\n\nBUCKET=\"$(date +%Y%m%d-%H 2>/dev/null)\"\n[ -z \"$BUCKET\" ] && BUCKET=\"unbucketed-$$\"\nMARKER=\"$MEMORY_DIR/.adr-staleness-fired-${BUCKET}\"\nCACHE=\"$MEMORY_DIR/.adr-staleness-cache-${SID}\"\n\n# Per-session 5-min cache (perf budget).\nif [ -f \"$CACHE\" ]; then\n  CACHE_MTIME=$(stat -c %Y \"$CACHE\" 2>/dev/null || stat -f %m \"$CACHE\" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)\n  AGE=$(( $(date +%s) - CACHE_MTIME ))\n  if [ \"$AGE\" -lt 300 ]; then\n    echo \"[$TS] project-md-adr-staleness: CACHE-HIT age=${AGE}s session=$SID\" >> \"$HOOK_LOG\" 2>/dev/null || true\n    exit 0\n  fi\nfi\n\n# Cleanup stale hour-bucket markers (L-S108-1 prevention) — also drops legacy\n# .project-md-staleness-fired-* markers from pre-rename predecessor.\nfor old_marker in \"$MEMORY_DIR\"/.adr-staleness-fired-* \"$MEMORY_DIR\"/.project-md-staleness-fired-*; do\n  [ -f \"$old_marker\" ] || continue\n  case \"$old_marker\" in\n    *\".adr-staleness-fired-${BUCKET}\") ;;\n    *) rm -f \"$old_marker\" 2>/dev/null || true ;;\n  esac\ndone\n\n# Idempotent: bail if already fired this hour-bucket.\n[ -f \"$MARKER\" ] && exit 0\n\n# Bail gracefully if project.md or decisions/ missing.\nif [ ! -f \"$PROJECT_MD\" ] || [ ! -d \"$DECISIONS_DIR\" ]; then\n  touch \"$MARKER\" 2>/dev/null || true\n  echo \"session=$SID ts=$TS state=NO-FILES detail=project-md-or-decisions-dir-missing\" > \"$CACHE\" 2>/dev/null || true\n  exit 0\nfi\n\nset +o pipefail\n\n# Find newest ADR — accept both production naming (NNN-*.md) AND backward-compat (D-*.md).\n# Original hook used only `D-*.md` which matched ZERO files (M-S176-1 root cause).\nNEWEST_ADR_INFO=$(find \"$DECISIONS_DIR\" -maxdepth 1 -type f \\\n                  \\( -name '[0-9][0-9][0-9]-*.md' -o -name 'D-*.md' \\) \\\n                  -printf '%T@\\t%f\\n' 2>/dev/null | sort -rn | head -1)\n\nNEWEST_ADR_TS=$(echo \"$NEWEST_ADR_INFO\" | cut -f1)\nNEWEST_ADR_NAME=$(echo \"$NEWEST_ADR_INFO\" | cut -f2)\n\n# Empty decisions/ → graceful bail (no ADRs yet to compare against).\nif [ -z \"$NEWEST_ADR_TS\" ] || [ -z \"$NEWEST_ADR_NAME\" ]; then\n  touch \"$MARKER\" 2>/dev/null || true\n  echo \"session=$SID ts=$TS state=GREEN detail=no-adr-files newest_adr=\" > \"$CACHE\" 2>/dev/null || true\n  echo \"[$TS] project-md-adr-staleness: state=GREEN detail=no-adr-files session=$SID\" >> \"$HOOK_LOG\" 2>/dev/null || true\n  exit 0\nfi\n\nPROJECT_MTIME=$(find \"$PROJECT_MD\" -printf '%T@\\n' 2>/dev/null)\n[ -z \"$PROJECT_MTIME\" ] && PROJECT_MTIME=0\n\nSTATE=\"GREEN\"\nSEVERITY=\"LOW\"\nDELTA_HOURS=\"0.0\"\nWARN_COUNT=0\n\n# Compare floats via awk — bash arithmetic doesn't handle floats.\nOLDER=$(awk -v p=\"$PROJECT_MTIME\" -v a=\"$NEWEST_ADR_TS\" 'BEGIN{print (p < a) ? 1 : 0}')\nif [ \"$OLDER\" = \"1\" ]; then\n  DELTA_HOURS=$(awk -v p=\"$PROJECT_MTIME\" -v a=\"$NEWEST_ADR_TS\" 'BEGIN{printf \"%.1f\", (a - p) / 3600}')\n  OVER=$(awk -v d=\"$DELTA_HOURS\" -v t=\"$TOLERANCE_HOURS\" 'BEGIN{print (d > t) ? 1 : 0}')\n  if [ \"$OVER\" = \"1\" ]; Flags two\n# staleness modes:\n#   (A) Active phase appearing in current-execution.md not present (or\n#       wrong status) in project.md Phase Goals Tracker.\n#   (B) project.md mtime older than newest ADR in decisions/ (project.md\n#       must reflect every architectural decision per the file's own header).\n#\n# Per HH-C of 009-S48-harness-hardening-middle-phase.md.\n# Per L-S11-1 portability: bash + standard POSIX tools only.\n# Soft-warn exit 0 always; never blocks Stop chain.\n\nset -uo pipefail\ntrap 'exit 0' ERR\n\nPROJECT_DIR=\"${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}\"\nMEMORY_DIR=\"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory\"\nPROJECT_MD=\"$MEMORY_DIR/project.md\"\nCURRENT_EXEC=\"$MEMORY_DIR/current-execution.md\"\nDECISIONS_DIR=\"$MEMORY_DIR/decisions\"\n# L-S108-1 fix (S109): per-session marker MUST use hour-bucket, NEVER fallback constant.\n# CLAUDE_SESSION_ID empty for Stop hooks on Windows → fallback \"default\" shared across\n# ALL sessions → marker collision → permanent idempotency lockout (M-S108-1 RCA: stale\n# .project-md-staleness-fired-default from S48g blocked hook S99-S108). SESSION_ID still\n# captured for log diagnostics (no fallback constant).\nSESSION_ID=\"${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID:-}\"\nBUCKET=\"$(date +%Y%m%d-%H 2>/dev/null)\"\n[ -z \"$BUCKET\" ] && BUCKET=\"unbucketed-$$\"\nMARKER=\"$MEMORY_DIR/.project-md-staleness-fired-${BUCKET}\"\nLOG=\"$MEMORY_DIR/.session-hooks.log\"\nTS=\"$(date -Iseconds 2>/dev/null || date '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S')\"\n\n# Cleanup stale markers from prior buckets (L-S108-1 prevention).\nfor old_marker in \"$MEMORY_DIR\"/.project-md-staleness-fired-*; do\n  [ -f \"$old_marker\" ] || continue\n  case \"$old_marker\" in\n    *\".project-md-staleness-fired-${BUCKET}\") ;;\n    *) rm -f \"$old_marker\" 2>/dev/null ;;\n  esac\ndone\n\n# Idempotent: bail if already fired this hour-bucket.\n[ -f \"$MARKER\" ] && exit 0\n\n# Bail gracefully if either file missing.\n[ ! -f \"$PROJECT_MD\" ] || [ ! -f \"$CURRENT_EXEC\" ] && { touch \"$MARKER\" 2>/dev/null || true; exit 0; }\n\n# Disable pipefail — legitimate grep-no-match returns 1 and would tip ERR trap.\nset +o pipefail\n\nWARN_COUNT=0\n\n# ============================================================================\n# Check A: phase status alignment\n# ============================================================================\n# Extract active phase number from current-execution.md \"**Phase**: N — ...\" line.\nACTIVE_PHASE=\"$(grep -m1 -E '^\\*\\*Phase\\*\\*:[[:space:]]*[0-9]' \"$CURRENT_EXEC\" 2>/dev/null \\\n                | sed -E 's/^\\*\\*Phase\\*\\*:[[:space:]]*([0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?).*/\\1/')\"\n\nif [ -n \"$ACTIVE_PHASE\" ]; then\n  # Check that project.md Phase Goals Tracker has a row for this phase with status\n  # matching reality. Phase Goals Tracker rows look like:\n  #   | 2.5 — Harness Hardening (NEW) | 8 tracks ... | IN PROGRESS | 2026-05-05 (S48) | - |\n  # We grep the row and inspect column 4 (status).\n  PHASE_ROW=\"$(grep -E \"^\\|[[:space:]]*${ACTIVE_PHASE}[[:space:]]+—\" \"$PROJECT_MD\" 2>/dev/null | head -1)\"\n\n  if [ -z \"$PHASE_ROW\" ]; then\n    echo \"[project-md-staleness-check] WARN: active Phase $ACTIVE_PHASE absent from project.md Phase Goals Tracker.\" >&2\n    echo \"[project-md-staleness-check] Action: add row to project.md table.\" >&2\n    WARN_COUNT=$(( WARN_COUNT + 1 ))\n  else\n    # Extract status column (3rd | -separated field after leading |).\n    PHASE_STATUS=\"$(echo \"$PHASE_ROW\" | awk -F'|' '{gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/,\"\",$4); print $4}')\"\n    case \"$PHASE_STATUS\" in\n      \"IN PROGRESS\"|\"DONE\"|\"PAUSED\"|\"NOT STARTED\"|\"BLOCKED\")\n        : # ok shape\n        ;;\n      *)\n        echo \"[project-md-staleness-check] WARN: Phase $ACTIVE_PHASE status='$PHASE_STATUS' not in {IN PROGRESS,DONE,PAUSED,NOT STARTED,BLOCKED}.\" >&2\n        WARN_COUNT=$(( WARN_COUNT + 1 ))\n        ;;\n    esac\n\n    # Cross-check: current-execution.md says active phase IN PROGRESS, project.md must agree.\n    # current-execution.md \"Track status\" section enumerates phases with ✅/🔵/⏸️.\n    if echo \"$PHASE_ROW\" | grep -q \"DONE\"; then\n      # If project.md says DONE but current-execution.md still calls it active → mismatch.\n      if grep -qE \"Phase ${ACTIVE_PHASE} (IN PROGRESS|🔵|in progress)\" \"$CURRENT_EXEC\" 2>/dev/null; then\n        echo \"[project-md-staleness-check] WARN: Phase $ACTIVE_PHASE = DONE in project.md but IN PROGRESS in current-execution.md.\" >&2\n        WARN_COUNT=$(( WARN_COUNT + 1 ))\n      fi\n    fi\n  fi\nfi\n\n# ============================================================================\n# Check B: project.md mtime vs newest ADR\n# ============================================================================\nif [ -d \"$DECISIONS_DIR\" ]; then\n  PROJECT_MTIME=\"$(find \"$PROJECT_MD\" -printf '%T@\\n' 2>/dev/null | head -1)\"\n  NEWEST_ADR_MTIME=\"$(find \"$DECISIONS_DIR\" -maxdepth 1 -name 'D-*.md' -type f -printf '%T@\\t%f\\n' 2>/dev/null \\\n                      | sort -rn | head -1)\"\n  NEWEST_ADR_TS=\"$(echo \"$NEWEST_ADR_MTIME\" | cut -f1)\"\n  NEWEST_ADR_NAME=\"$(echo \"$NEWEST_ADR_MTIME\" | cut -f2)\"\n\n  if [ -n \"$PROJECT_MTIME\" ] && [ -n \"$NEWEST_ADR_TS\" ]; then\n    # Compare floats via awk — bash arithmetic doesn't handle floats.\n    OLDER=\"$(awk -v p=\"$PROJECT_MTIME\" -v a=\"$NEWEST_ADR_TS\" 'BEGIN{print (p < a) ? 1 : 0}')\"\n    if [ \"$OLDER\" = \"1\" ]; then\n      DELTA_HOURS=\"$(awk -v p=\"$PROJECT_MTIME\" -v a=\"$NEWEST_ADR_TS\" 'BEGIN{printf \"%.1f\", (a - p) / 3600}')\"\n      # Tolerate <2h drift (ADR + project.md often updated minutes apart).\n      OVER=\"$(awk -v d=\"$DELTA_HOURS\" 'BEGIN{print (d > 2.0) ? 1 : 0}')\"\n      if [ \"$OVER\" = \"1\" ]; TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))\n  if [ \"$cond\" = \"1\" ] || [ \"$cond\" = \"true\" ]; then\n    PASS=$((PASS + 1))\n    echo \"  [PASS] $desc\"\n  else\n    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))\n    echo \"  [FAIL] $desc\"\n  fi\n}\n\nnew_tempdir() {\n  local d\n  d=$(mktemp -d -t adr-staleness-test-XXXXXX 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || echo \"/tmp/adr-staleness-$$-${RANDOM}\")\n  mkdir -p Firing-test for project-md-staleness-check.sh (Phase 3.5 T7 retrofit; S59).\n# Extended at S109 with TC7 — L-S108-1 stale-marker regression test.\n#\n# Hook purpose (HH-C.2 Stop): detect drift between project.md \"Phase Goals Tracker\"\n# and current-execution.md \"Active Focus Track\". Two staleness modes:\n#   (A) Active phase from current-execution absent (or wrong status) in project.md tracker\n#   (B) project.md mtime older than newest ADR by >2h\n# Idempotent per HOUR-BUCKET via marker file (L-S108-1; was per-session but\n# $CLAUDE_SESSION_ID empty on Windows → fallback-to-constant lockout).\n#\n# Test strategy: stage temp PROJECT_DIR with project.md + current-execution.md +\n# decisions/ fixtures; invoke hook; assert .session-hooks.log content reflects warns.\n#\n# 7 test cases:\n#   TC1 — both files missing → silent (graceful bail)\n#   TC2 — clean alignment (active phase exists with status IN PROGRESS) → silent\n#   TC3 — active phase absent from project.md → WARN\n#   TC4 — phase status DONE in project.md but IN PROGRESS in current-execution → WARN\n#   TC5 — project.md mtime > 2h older than newest ADR → WARN\n#   TC6 — project.md mtime < 2h older than newest ADR → silent (within tolerance)\n#   TC7 — L-S108-1 REGRESSION: stale cross-bucket + legacy \"default\" marker\n#         present → cleanup deletes both, current-bucket marker created\n#\n# Exit 0 = all assertions pass. Exit 1 = any assertion fail.\nset -euo pipefail\n\nSCRIPT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")\" && pwd)\"\nHOOK=\"$SCRIPT_DIR/../project-md-staleness-check.sh\"\n[ ! -f \"$HOOK\" ] && { echo \"FAIL: hook script not found at $HOOK\"; exit 1; }\n\nTEMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)\ntrap \"rm -rf $TEMPDIR\" EXIT\n\nLOG=\"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/.session-hooks.log\"\n\nrun_hook() {\n  local session_id=\"${1:-test-session-tc}\"\n  CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=\"$TEMPDIR\" CLAUDE_SESSION_ID=\"$session_id\" \\\n    bash \"$HOOK\" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n}\n\nclean_state() {\n  rm -rf \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace\"\n  mkdir -p \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/decisions\"\n}\n\ncurrent_marker() {\n  # Hour-bucket marker per L-S108-1 (matches hook's date +%Y%m%d-%H)\n  echo \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/.project-md-staleness-fired-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H)\"\n}\n\n# --- TC1: both files missing → silent (graceful bail) ---\nclean_state\nrun_hook \"tc1-session\"\nif [ -f \"$LOG\" ] && grep -q \"tc1-session\" \"$LOG\" 2>/dev/null; then\n  echo \"FAIL TC1: hook should silently exit when project.md/current-execution.md missing\"\n  cat \"$LOG\"\n  exit 1\nfi\necho \"PASS TC1: missing files → silent\"\n\n# --- TC2: clean alignment → silent ---\nclean_state\ncat > \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md\" <<EOF\n# Current Execution\n\n**Phase**: 3.5 — Harness Deepening\nEOF\ncat > \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/project.md\" <<EOF\n# Project State\n\n| Phase | Tracks | Status | Started | Closed |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 3.5 — Harness Deepening | 8 tracks | IN PROGRESS | 2026-05-05 | - |\nEOF\nrun_hook \"tc2-session\"\nif [ -f \"$LOG\" ] && grep -q \"tc2-session\" \"$LOG\" 2>/dev/null; then\n  echo \"FAIL TC2: clean alignment should NOT emit warns\"\n  cat \"$LOG\"\n  exit 1\nfi\necho \"PASS TC2: clean alignment → silent\"\n\n# --- TC3: active phase absent from project.md → WARN ---\nclean_state\ncat > \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md\" <<EOF\n# Current Execution\n\n**Phase**: 9 — Future Phase\nEOF\ncat > \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/project.md\" <<EOF\n# Project State\n\n| Phase | Tracks | Status | Started | Closed |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 3.5 — Harness Deepening | 8 tracks | IN PROGRESS | 2026-05-05 | - |\nEOF\nrun_hook \"tc3-session\"\nif [ ! -f \"$LOG\" ] || ! grep -q \"tc3-session\" \"$LOG\"; then\n  echo \"FAIL TC3: expected WARN log entry for missing phase\"\n  cat \"$LOG\" 2>&1 || echo \"(no log)\"\n  exit 1\nfi\n# Should mention phase=9\nif ! grep -q \"phase=9\" \"$LOG\"; then\n  echo \"FAIL TC3: log should mention phase=9 in warn entry\"\n  cat \"$LOG\"\n  exit 1\nfi\necho \"PASS TC3: active phase absent from project.md → WARN\"\n\n# --- TC4: project.md says DONE but current-execution.md says IN PROGRESS → WARN ---\nclean_state\ncat > \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md\" <<EOF\n# Current Execution\n\n**Phase**: 2 — Done Phase\n\nPhase 2 IN PROGRESS active here.\nEOF\ncat > \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/project.md\" <<EOF\n# Project State\n\n| Phase | Tracks | Status | Started | Closed |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 2 — Done Phase | 5 tracks | DONE | 2026-04-01 | 2026-04-15 |\nEOF\nrun_hook \"tc4-session\"\nif [ ! -f \"$LOG\" ] || ! grep -q \"tc4-session\" \"$LOG\"; then\n  echo \"FAIL TC4: expected WARN log entry for status mismatch\"\n  cat \"$LOG\" 2>&1 || echo \"(no log)\"\n  exit 1\nfi\necho \"PASS TC4: project.md DONE vs current-execution.md IN PROGRESS → WARN\"\n\n# --- TC5: project.md mtime > 2h older than newest ADR → WARN ---\nclean_state\ncat > \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md\" <<EOF\n# Current Execution\n\n**Phase**: 3.5 — Harness Deepening\nEOF\ncat > \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/project.md\" <<EOF\n# Project State\n\n| Phase | Tracks | Status | Started | Closed |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 3.5 — Harness Deepening | 8 tracks | IN PROGRESS | 2026-05-05 | - |\nEOF\n# Make project.md 5 hours old; ADR is fresh.\ntouch -d \"5 hours ago\" \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/project.md\"\ncat > \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/decisions/D-031-test-adr.md\" <<EOF\n# D-031 test ADR\nEOF\n# ADR mtime = now (default); project.md mtime = 5h ago → delta = 5h > 2h tolerance.\nrun_hook \"tc5-session\"\nif [ ! -f \"$LOG\" ] || ! grep -q \"tc5-session\" \"$LOG\"; then\n  echo \"FAIL TC5: expected WARN log entry for mtime drift\"\n  cat \"$LOG\" 2>&1 || echo \"(no log)\"\n  exit 1\nfi\necho \"PASS TC5: project.md > 2h older than newest ADR → WARN\"\n\n# --- TC6: project.md mtime < 2h older than ADR → silent (within tolerance) ---\nclean_state\ncat > \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md\" <<EOF\n# Current Execution\n\n**Phase**: 3.5 — Harness Deepening\nEOF\ncat > \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/project.md\" <<EOF\n# Project State\n\n| Phase | Tracks | Status | Started | Closed |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 3.5 — Harness Deepening | 8 tracks | IN PROGRESS | 2026-05-05 | - |\nEOF\n# Make project.md 30 minutes old; ADR is fresh — within 2h tolerance.\ntouch -d \"30 minutes ago\" \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/project.md\"\ncat > \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/decisions/D-031-test-adr.md\" <<EOF\n# D-031 test ADR\nEOF\nrun_hook \"tc6-session\"\nif [ -f \"$LOG\" ] && grep -q \"tc6-session\" \"$LOG\" 2>/dev/null; then\n  echo \"FAIL TC6: 30min mtime delta within 2h tolerance — should NOT WARN\"\n  cat \"$LOG\"\n  exit 1\nfi\necho \"PASS TC6: project.md mtime within 2h tolerance → silent\"\n\n# --- TC7: L-S108-1 REGRESSION — stale cross-bucket + legacy 'default' marker ---\n# Reproduces M-S108-1 sister-bug: hook stuck because .project-md-staleness-fired-default\n# (legacy CLAUDE_SESSION_ID:-default fallback marker) blocked all subsequent sessions.\n# Fix asserts cleanup loop deletes BOTH stale-bucket and legacy markers + work happens.\nclean_state\ncat > \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md\" <<EOF\n# Current Execution\n\n**Phase**: 9 — Future Phase\nEOF\ncat > \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/project.md\" <<EOF\n# Project State\n\n| Phase | Tracks | Status | Started | Closed |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 3.5 — Harness Deepening | 8 tracks | IN PROGRESS | 2026-05-05 | - |\nEOF\n# Plant stale Jan-2026 hour-bucket marker (different bucket from current)\ntouch \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/.project-md-staleness-fired-20260105-13\"\n# Plant LEGACY fallback marker (the EXACT M-S108-1 sister-bug filename)\ntouch \"$TEMPDIR/agent-workspace/memory/.project-md-staleness-fired-default\"\nrun_hook \"tc7-session\"\nif [ ! -f \"$LOG\" ] || ! grep -q \"tc7-session\" \"$LOG\"; Keep concise (target <2500 tokens).\n\n## Identity\n\nYou are **Claude Code**, the primary engineering partner for the StockForge project — an AI-first investment advisory system for the Vietnamese stock market.\n\n**Primary user**: Project owner (self-use + small trusted circle).\n**Stack**: Python primary + Postgres 16 (TimescaleDB + pgvector) + Redis + Claude API. Streamlit for dashboard. NestJS only when public API needed.\n\n---\n\n## Core Principles (Karpathy 4)\n\n**P1. Think Before Coding.** State assumptions. Surface tradeoffs. Push back when simpler approach exists. Stop when confused.\n\n**P2. Simplicity First.** Minimum code that solves the problem. No speculative features. If 200 lines could be 50, rewrite.\n\n**P3. Surgical Changes.** Touch only what the task requires. Match existing style. Every changed line traces to the task.\n\n**P4. Goal-Driven Execution.** Transform imperative → verifiable goals with concrete success criteria.\n\nFull detail: `agent-workspace/constitution/karpathy-principles.md`.\n\n---\n\n## StockForge-Specific Hard Rules (read CHARTER for context)\n\n- **NO LLM math.** LLM never outputs numbers it computed. Every number comes from code with verified inputs. LLM only interprets.\n- **Every claim has source + as-of date.** No exceptions. Hallucinated numbers in finance = real money lost.\n- **Position sizing & risk management are deterministic code.** LLM cannot override max position size, sector concentration, stop loss rules.\n- **Output is structured, not narrative.** Use trade-off matrices, multi-criteria, never single \"buy/sell\" score.\n- **Adversarial by default.** Any thesis output includes bear case explicitly. Single-perspective output is anti-pattern.\n- **Calibration over confidence.** Confidence claims must trace to historical hit rate, not to model \"feeling certain\".\n- **No insider information.** Public sources only. No paid leaks, no insider channels.\n- **Frame as research aid, not financial advice.** Use \"thesis exploration\", \"consideration\" — not \"recommendation\", \"buy\", \"sell\".\n\n---\n\n## Session Protocol\n\n### Start\n1. Read `agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md` → resolve active track\n2. Read `agent-workspace/memory/project.md` → project state\n3. Read last 3 files in `agent-workspace/memory/sessions/` → recent context\n4. Check `agent-workspace/session-plans/pending/` for matching brief\n5. Run VBW protocol before writing any spec/test/code\n\n### End\n1. Update `agent-workspace/memory/project.md` (if architectural decisions made)\n2. Write `agent-workspace/memory/sessions/YYYY-MM-DD-session-N.md`\n3. Update `agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md` (status, next session)\n4. If learned rule emerged → append to `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md`\n5. If thesis logged this session → ensure entry in `agent-workspace/memory/thesis-log/`\n6. Update `agent-workspace/memory/mistake-log.md` with new M-S<N>-<M> entries OR explicitly state \"no mistakes this session\" in the session log (enforced by `session-end-checklist-linter.sh`)\n7. If a NEW ADR landed this session → verify `project.md` Phase Goals Tracker still matches `current-execution.md` Active Focus Track Phase status (enforced by `project-md-staleness-check.sh`)\n8. (auto) Stop-hook `profile-template-auto-populate.sh` appends a sample row to the matching `agent-workspace/memory/self-awareness/profiles/<model>-<effort>-<task_class>.md` card\n9. (auto) Stop-hook `promotion-cycle-trigger.sh` HARD-BLOCKs at next SessionStart if ≥8 new lessons accumulated since last `promote-rule` dispatch — schedule a promote-rule subagent dispatch in the next session if blocked\n\n---\n\n## Constitution (always applicable)\n\n| File | Enforces |\n|---|---|\n| `agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md` | Layer boundaries, BC rules (9 BCs for stock domain) |\n| `agent-workspace/constitution/invariants.md` | Stock-specific invariants (numbers, citations, no LLM math) |\n| `agent-workspace/constitution/vbw-protocol.md` | Verify-Before-Write checkpoints |\n| `agent-workspace/constitution/drift-signals.md` | DR1-DR12 drift detection |\n| `agent-workspace/constitution/session-budgets.md` | Token budget rules |\n| `agent-workspace/constitution/boundaries.md` | What you cannot do without human approval |\n| `agent-workspace/constitution/financial-data-protocol.md` | Stock-specific data integrity rules |\n\nRead these when relevant to current task.\n\n---\n\n## Hard Rules (general)\n\n- **Domain layer has ZERO framework dependency.** Pure Python in `packages/domain/`. No FastAPI, no Pydantic in domain (use dataclasses).\n- **Cross-BC communication via contracts only.** Never direct import between bounded contexts.\n- **VBW Protocol mandatory before writing specs/tests/code.** Read actual source, not memory.\n- **Never edit `obsidian-vault/raw/`.** Immutable. All writes go to `wiki/`.\n- **Never modify `PROJECT_CHARTER.md`.** Requires explicit human revision with version bump.\n- **Never modify files in `agent-workspace/constitution/` without explicit human approval.**\n- **Agents MUST NOT `git commit` unless user explicitly requests.** Stage changes, report, let user decide.\n- **User prompt overrides ALL defaults.** If user says \"skip X\", that trumps any skill/workflow.\n- **Context-threshold band (per D-004 — Opus 4.7 recalibrated)**: 180K wind-down (auto-prep handoff) / 220K cliff (auto-reboot via session-self-reboot.sh) / 250K hard_cap (mandatory split). Operational defaults in `scripts/hooks/budget-watchdog.sh`. Re-evaluate empirically after 10 sessions or on Anthropic model/policy change.\n- **Deterministic gates (mypy, pytest, ruff) must pass before commit.** Max 3 retry before escalate.\n- **Tracking retention (per S99 RCA Layer 1; Q-RCA-1 = A)**: `current-execution.md` ≤ 5 sessions inline / ≤ 200 LOC; `agent-notes.md` digest only / ≤ 700 LOC; `mistake-log.md` digest only / ≤ 200 LOC; `component-telemetry.jsonl` ≤ 10 MB (weekly rotate via `telemetry-rotate.sh`, retain 4 weeks). Cap breaches: WARN-only via `tracking-retention.sh` Stop hook; manual archive to dated file. Working-memory budget per `agent-workspace/proposals/memory-tiers.md` § Tier 1 = ≤ 20 KB combined for routine load.\n- **Ritual demotion (per S99 RCA Layer 5; Q-RCA-5 + Q-RCA-7 = A)**: per-session rituals (audit / re-scan / refresh) MUST track catch-rate. Catch-rate = 0 over 3+ consecutive sessions ⇒ promote-to-hook OR demote-to-passive OR retire. Refinement-of-rule (lesson-about-lesson) is AP-23 RED FLAG: 2nd instance mandates promote-or-retire (not inline accumulation).\n\n---\n\n## Dispatch Rules\n\nDo NOT hardcode phase/task paths from memory. Route through:\n- `agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md` is the single source of truth\n- Short prompts (\"session N\", \"phase X\") resolve there\n\n---\n\n## Session Types (choose at start)\n\n| Type | Budget | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|\n| PLAN | 50-80K | Architect subagent, produces session plan |\n| FOCUSED IMPL | 100-150K | Dev, 1-3 tasks from plan |\n| MULTI-TASK IMPL | 150-250K | Dev, 4-10 tasks from plan |\n| VERIFY | 30-60K | Verifier subagent, adversarial review |\n| RECOVERY | 80-150K | Revert + re-plan after failure |\n| THESIS | 60-100K | Multi-perspective adversarial analysis on a stock |\n| INGEST | 40-80K | Process new data sources into KB |\n| POST-MORTEM | 30-50K | Review thesis outcomes, update calibration |\n\n**Never mix PLAN and IMPL in same session.** (Session 4 catastrophic failure mode.)\n**THESIS sessions are read-only on code.** Output goes to `agent-workspace/memory/thesis-log/`.\n\n---\n\n## Quality Gates\n\n**Tier 1 — Deterministic** (per commit, auto-block on fail):\nmypy --strict, pytest, ruff, drift-signals HIGH, dependency cycle check.\n\n**Tier 2 — Probabilistic** (per merge, separate agent):\nSpec alignment, architecture boundaries, UL consistency, code review, **calibration drift check**.\n\n**Tier 3 — Human** (per phase boundary or strategic decision):\nArchitectural decisions, API contracts, eval regression sign-off, **thesis quality review**.\n\n---\n\n## Common Anti-Patterns (avoid)\n\n- **LLM generating numbers.** `\"Based on my analysis, ROE is approximately 18%\"` — WRONG. Code must compute from data.\n- **Single-perspective thesis.** Always include bear case, even when bullish.\n- **Confident output without calibration data.** \"High confidence\" requires historical hit rate, not just model belief.\n- **Recommending stocks user already owns.** Check portfolio first; surface conflicts (confirmation bias risk).\n- **Over-fitting to recent backtest.** VN market regimes change; performance in 2021-2022 doesn't predict 2024.\n- Load entire codebase before starting (Session 4 failure) — use just-in-time loading\n- Mix plan + implement in same session (catastrophic)\n- Same-agent self-review (echo chamber) — use separate agent for Tier 2 gate\n- Write code from convention/memory — use VBW protocol\n- Refactor adjacent unrelated code (violates P3)\n- Speculative features \"for future flexibility\" (violates P2)\n\n---\n\n## Key References\n\n- **Project state**: `agent-workspace/memory/project.md`\n- **Execution router**: `agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md`\n- **Learned rules**: `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md`\n- **Thesis log**: `agent-workspace/memory/thesis-log/`\n- **Calibration data**: `agent-workspace/calibration/`\n- **Charter (immutable)**: `PROJECT_CHARTER.md`\n- **Operating manual**: `AGENT_OPERATING_MANUAL.md`\n- **Spec template**: `SPEC_TEMPLATE.md`\n- **Ubiquitous language**: `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md`\n- **Skills**: `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`\n- **Commands**: `.claude/commands/*.md`\n- **Subagents**: `.claude/agents/*.md`\n\n---\n\n## First Interaction\n\nIf user is starting fresh, run `/session-start` to load state and suggest next actions.\nIf this is the very first session ever → guide them through `docs/DAY_1_CHECKLIST.md`.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":54,"oldLines":7,"newStart":54,"newLines":7,"lines":[" 4.
